AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND
AbstractText.content: Irritability and emotion regulation are both important transdiagnostic factors that contribute to the development of internalizing symptoms during adolescence. The current study examined whether emotion regulation mediates the relationship between irritability and internalizing symptoms.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: To examine this relationship we analysed the indirect effect of irritability (measured using a single item from the Goldberg Mania Questionnaire) on internalizing symptoms (anxiety and depression) via the mediator, emotion regulation (Difficulties in Emotion Regulation Scale) in 112 adolescent females.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: Mediation analysis, using bootstrapping, showed a significant indirect effect and suggests that the relationship between irritability and internalizing symptoms is mediated by emotion dysregulation.

AbstractText.Label: LIMITATIONS
AbstractText.content: These include measuring irritability using a single item and employing a cross sectional design.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: These novel findings add to our understanding of the processes and mechanisms by which irritability contributes to the development of internalizing symptoms.
